# Autocomplete at the shell's prompt (zsh with shell integration, an empty
# ZDOTDIR: no plugin of the user's draws suggestions of its own).
#
# A command the shell ran is remembered; typing its start shows the rest
# dimmed after the cursor (ghost text) — and nothing more reaches the shell
# until a key takes it: → whole, ⌥→ a word.
type:echo ac-$((40+2)) tail-word
key:enter
wait:1.0
action:clear_screen
wait:1.0
expect-not:ac-42
type:echo ac
expect-ghost:-$((40+2)) tail-word
# The shell has only what was typed.
expect-not:echo ac-
# ⌥→ takes a word, → the rest.
key:alt+right
expect-ghost: tail-word
expect:echo ac-$((40+2))
key:right
expect-ghost:none
key:enter
expect:ac-42 tail-word
# Typing on past what it suggested: none.
type:echo acx
expect-ghost:none
key:ctrl+u
# The shell's own completions listed under the line (zsh's Tab): none,
# the arrows there are the shell's.
type:ls /usr/bin >/dev/null
key:enter
wait:0.5
type:ls /usr/
expect-ghost:bin >/dev/null
key:tab
wait:0.5
expect:libexec
expect-ghost:none
key:ctrl+u
key:ctrl+l
wait:0.5
# In a program (no prompt): none, and → is the program's.
type:cat
key:enter
wait:0.5
type:echo ac
expect-ghost:none
key:ctrl+c
wait:0.5
# Lines that start with a space, or look like they hold a secret, aren't remembered.
type: echo spaced-$((1+1))
key:enter
type:export MY_TOKEN=s3cr3t
key:enter
wait:0.5
type:echo sp
expect-ghost:none
key:ctrl+u
type:export MY_T
expect-ghost:none
key:ctrl+u
# The completion list (⌃⇧Space): the word's subcommands, chosen with the
# arrows, typed with Tab; Esc closes it.
type:git ch
key:ctrl+shift+space
expect-completions:> checkout
expect-completions:cherry-pick
key:down
expect-completions:> cherry-pick
key:escape
expect-completions:none
key:ctrl+shift+space
expect-completions:> checkout
key:tab
expect-completions:none
expect:git checkout
key:ctrl+u
# Typing on with it open: it follows what's typed.
type:git c
key:ctrl+shift+space
expect-completions:> commit
expect-completions:clone
type:h
expect-completions:> checkout
key:escape
key:ctrl+u
